entries.content: S517 measures the Productive Capital Stock (K*) — the fixed capital stock employed in productive sectors. In the Shaikh-Tonak framework, this is the capital stock corresponding to sectors that produce use-values and surplus value (agriculture, mining, construction, manufacturing, transportation, communications, utilities, and trade).

Registry specifies a single construction step: load subseries S517-A, which is 'BEA Fixed Assets 4.1 Line 1' covering 1925-2024 in billions of USD. The loader is L01 and processor is P02. Wave 2 assignment indicates this is a foundational series loaded early in the pipeline.

S517-A sources from BEA Fixed Assets Table 4.1, Line 1 — Current-Cost Net Stock of Private Fixed Assets. This table provides the net stock of private fixed assets by industry. The productive capital stock requires filtering to productive industries only (per the Shaikh-Tonak sector classification).
entries.source_ref: series_registry.json subseries S517-A; BEA Fixed Assets tables

entries.content: K* enters profit rate calculations as the denominator: r = S*/K* (the Marxian general rate of profit). It also appears in capital-output ratios and organic composition of capital. Chapter 5 develops these measures as part of the overall framework for measuring the wealth of nations.
entries.source_ref: ST_1994, Ch5 and Ch9 profit rate analysis

entries.content: No extension is specified (extension: null) — the BEA Fixed Assets data already extends to 2024, providing continuous modern coverage. Status is book_period_validated.
the Marxian general rate of profit r*, defined here as the ratio of surplus value to total fixed capital K
entries.context: Verbatim from Section 5.5 'Marxian, Average, and Corporate Rates of Profit' — establishes K (which S517 operationalizes as Productive Capital Stock K*) as the denominator of r*. This is the canonical citation for why S517 exists in the registry.

entries.content: More properly, one should add the stock of circulating capital (i.e., inventories of raw materials and goods in process, which are the stock equivalents of C* and V*, or M and W in the orthodox case) to the stock of fixed capital. But consistent data on the former are not readily available.
entries.context: Verbatim Footnote 16 — acknowledged scope limitation of S517. ST explicitly restrict K to fixed capital because circulating-capital stock data are unavailable. This caveat must be inherited by the DPR/EPR for S517 and surfaces in V03 validation as a known scope boundary.

entries.content: We also estimate the value composition of (fixed) capital C*/V* = K/V*, as well as the materialized composition of (fixed) capital C*/(V* + S*) = K/(V* + S*). All variables are in current dollars, including the capital stock that is measured at current replacement costs.
entries.context: Verbatim — pins down two critical operational properties of S517: (1) K is measured at current replacement cost (matching BEA Fixed Assets Table 4.1 'Current-Cost Net Stock' convention), and (2) K is used not only in r* but also in the value composition C*/V* and the materialized composition C*/(V*+S*). This justifies the registry's cross_references to S501/S505/S506.

entries.content: all measured ratios are adjusted for cyclical fluctuations by means of a measure of capacity utilization developed in Shaikh (1987, 1992a).
entries.context: Verbatim — ST do not use raw K in r* but K adjusted for capacity utilization. For S517, this means downstream profit-rate constructions must apply the capacity-utilization adjustment from Shaikh (1987, 1992a); S517 itself is unadjusted current-cost net stock, with the adjustment applied at the ratio stage in V03 or in the P02 of profit-rate series.

entries.content: The Marxian general rate of profit r*, defined here as the ratio of surplus value to total fixed capital K.
entries.context: Section 5.5, p. 122: K (total fixed capital, current dollars, current replacement costs) is the operational denominator for r*. S517 loads K* from BEA Fixed Assets Table 4.1 Line 1 to serve this role.

entries.content: More properly, one should add the stock of circulating capital (i.e., inventories of raw materials and goods in process, which are the stock equivalents of C* and V*, or M and W in the orthodox case) to the stock of fixed capital. But consistent data on the former are not readily available.
entries.context: Section 5.5, Footnote 16, p. 122: acknowledged limitation of S517 — it captures fixed capital only, not the full K + circulating capital that would ideally appear in the denominator of r*.

entries.content: All variables are in current dollars, including the capital stock that is measured at current replacement costs.
entries.context: Section 5.5, p. 122: confirms the BEA Fixed Assets convention (current-cost replacement) that S517 inherits from Table 4.1 Line 1.

methodology_summary: Productive Capital Stock (K*) loaded from BEA Fixed Assets Table 4.1 Line 1 (1925-2024). Used in profit rate calculations as the capital denominator (r = S*/K*).
known_issues: Sector filtering for productive-only industries not yet documented in detail
BEA Fixed Assets industry classifications may differ from the original 85 IO sectors used in the book
